_doc: Segment-A trail map parameters. Every entry is {value, why}. load_config() strips the 'why'.

navmap_free_dilation_m.why: A pose counts as 'on the paved/nav-map area' if a FREE (254) PGM cell lies within this radius: absorbs the 0.1 m PGM quantisation and the ~0.3-0.5 m offset between a hand-held scanner and the walker's feet. Exit/entry moved by <1.2 m of path for 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 m (see segment.json dilation_sensitivity).

dilation_sensitivity_m.why: Report how the exit/entry depend on the dilation choice.

approach_m.why: Brief: ~10 m of approach on the paved area at each end.

work_margin_raw_m.why: Raw path length processed beyond exit/entry before cutting, so the 10 m approach is cut from an already cleaned line.

pause_min_step_m.why: Pause removal: a pose is kept only after the scanner moved >=0.2 m in XY (stationary jitter is a few cm; equals the station spacing).

loop_close_radius_m.why: Back-and-forth detection: returning within 1.0 m (about half a trail width) of an already kept point closes a loop.

loop_close_dz_m.why: Loop closure also needs |dz|<0.5 m so that vertically separated trail passes (switchbacks, bridges) are never merged; a person's scanner height varies <0.3 m between passes.

loop_min_arc_m.why: Only an excursion of >=2 m walked path (2x the closure radius) is a loop; normal forward walking never returns within 1 m after 2 m.

loop_max_arc_m.why: Upper bound on a removable excursion; the whole trail loop (~850 m) can never be pruned. Longest pruned excursion is reported.

smoothing_sigma_m.why: Gaussian smoothing along arc length removes walking sway (+-0.1 m at step frequency) but keeps bends of radius >~1.5 m.

station_spacing_m.why: Brief: resample at 0.2 m XY arc length (same as the existing map contract).

res_m.why: Brief and existing map contract: 0.1 m cells.

coverage_radius_m.why: Map content is kept within 12 m of the centreline (brief: >=10 m; BEV reaches 6 m ahead / 4 m sideways and sensors 8 m, from a robot up to 0.75 m + 0.35 m off-route before 'wrong-way' termination). Outside: known=0, unsupported, empty atlas.

crop_radius_m.why: Point crop radius around centreline AND raw walked poses: coverage 12 m + 2 m so neighbourhood filters (<=1.5 m) are not edge-biased inside the covered area.

bbox_margin_m.why: Dense grid = route bounding box + 12.5 m (coverage radius + 0.5 m).

layer_thickness_m.why: Lowest layer = lowest point with >= layer_min_points points within 5 cm above it in the cell (5 cm ~ 2-3 sigma of LiDAR range noise on hard ground).

layer_min_points.why: Rejects isolated single low returns (multipath/noise) while keeping sparse ground under vegetation (median density ~50 points per 0.1 m cell). No normal filter: the lowest return of a trunk/wall/riser column is its base, i.e. ground; provider normals are unreliable in vegetation.

vegetation_slab_m.why: Slab above the lowest layer used for the return-concentration test (grass/fern height scale).

bare_concentration_min.why: Bare soil/concrete: most returns in the 0.3 m slab lie in the lowest 5 cm. Below 0.5 the layer is diffuse (vegetation).

median_window.why: Pit/spike test identical to the old proxy (5x5 = 0.5 m median).

median_tolerance_m.why: Unchanged ground pit/spike rejection: deviation >=0.25 m from the 0.5 m median, not a riser-height capability. A broad tread stays near its local median; final support uses terrain.max_step_m.

envelope_radius_m.why: Lower-envelope cone radius (about half the robot length): object tops are judged against ground seen within 0.6 m.

envelope_slope_deg.why: Unchanged 45 degree lower-envelope cone for rejecting diffuse vegetation/object tops. This is a ground extraction prior, not the sustained locomotion grade; it does not reject bare ground solely for exceeding 45 degrees.

vegetation_top_min_m.why: A lowest layer >=0.25 m above the 45-deg envelope AND diffuse (concentration<0.5) is a vegetation/object top: ground there is unobserved (stays unknown unless within the 0.2 m gap fill).

connect_max_dz_m.why: Ground-surface extraction continuity: 0.30 m (confirmed 0.28 m riser plus 0.02 m ground noise). This reconstructs ground only; support still requires the uninflated 0.28 m limit.

min_component_area_m2.why: Observed-ground islands not connected to the walked-path surface are kept only if >=1 m^2 (rejects isolated flat object tops such as rock/post tops).

interpolate_radius_m.why: Old proxy value: gaps up to 0.2 m are interpolated (nearest); larger gaps stay unknown/unsupported.

walked_cell_radius_m.why: Cells within 0.15 m of a moving raw pose are 'under the walked path' (scanner XY ~ foot position within a stride).

device_height_radius_m.why: Ground under a pose for the device-height estimate: median lowest layer within 0.2 m.

device_height_min_speed_mps.why: Pauses excluded: during long stops the operator lowered the scanner (h 0.3-1.2 m for 20-40 s at s=132, 351, 533, 649, 720 m).

prior_fill_under_path.why: Brief: ground under the walked path ~= scanner z - device height; used only for walked-path cells whose ground is otherwise unknown.

prior_tolerance_m.why: Walked-path seeds must lie within 0.5 m of scanner z - device height (~4 robust sigma of the measured device-height spread, 0.12 m).

second_layer_gap_m.why: A second surface layer in the same cell must start >= 0.3 m above the lowest one (distinct surface, not the same ground).

sub_surface_min_drop_m.why: Replace a disconnected lowest layer only when the walked-connected upper layer is >=0.50 m higher; larger than the confirmed 0.28 m riser, preserving real shallow terrain.

deck_over_void.why: Fix C: under walked cells whose ground lies more than prior_tolerance_m below (scanner z - device height), a near-horizontal bare layer of returns within prior_tolerance_m of that walked surface and >= second_layer_gap_m above the ground is the walking surface (bridge deck / culvert cover); the lower returns are the void below it.

deck_connect_max_dz_m.why: Fix C: the deck is grown over 8-neighbours whose deck layer lies within 5 cm of the neighbouring deck height (= layer_thickness_m, 2-3 sigma LiDAR range noise on hard surfaces): a continuous surface, not a separate object. 'Near-horizontal' itself = majority of layer returns with |normal_z| >= cos(deck_max_grade_deg 35) (deck-recognition geometry, independent of locomotion grade); 'bare' = layer / 0.3 m slab returns >= bare_concentration_min (not vegetation).

deck_max_distance_m.why: Fix C: deck growth limited to 2 m from the walked line: covers the +-0.75 m acceptance band plus the robot half-length 0.515 m and half-width 0.29 m (1.56 m) with one cell to spare; the footbridge at s 718.8 is 1.4 m wide between its rails, so its edges are reached.

deck_max_grade_deg.why: Deck identification retains the previous local-normal threshold (cos 35 degrees). This identifies a near-horizontal bridge surface, not locomotion capability; do not widen it when changing the sustained 1 m grade capability.

max_step_m.why: User confirmed 2026-11-16: M1 official loco stair mode traverses a 0.28 m riser. A-trail flight 2 (s 9.1-14.5 m) measured maximum 0.27707 m; round up to centimetres, with no extra capability margin. Generic capability and measured-tread support use this limit. The restored trail prior is recorded separately from quantitative capability.

step_radius_m.why: 8 neighbours plus axis central differences across 0.20 m on the 0.10 m grid. A 47 degree plane rises 0.2145 m across 0.20 m, below the 0.28 m riser limit; a 0.40 m edge remains unsupported even if the 1 m grade fit averages it out.

max_grade_deg.why: User confirmed 2026-11-16: a 47 degree grade measured over 1 m is traversable. Applied to a least-squares plane over a 1.0 m diameter disc, not to the old 0.6 m disc or sensor one-cell derivative. On a plane this equals rise/run=tan(47)=1.07237; on irregular terrain it is a stated model of the confirmed scale, not an exact conversion from local 35 degrees.

grade_radius_m.why: 1.0 m diameter support for least-squares ground-plane grade, matching the confirmed measurement scale and sensor terrain.grade_baseline_m=1.0. Known samples only; insufficient map coverage remains unsupported. Short-baseline step test prevents smoothing across cliffs.

trail_terrain_exemption.why: Restore the user declaration (CLAUDE.md section 1): A-trail terrain is traversable in M1 stair mode. Restrict exemption to known trail-connected ground within the existing 0.75 m zone. Keep the original 35 degree cross-grade guard, plus separately measured tread-surface support; neither bypasses hard collision or fills unknown ground.

trail_zone_halfwidth_m.why: Trail zone = within 0.75 m of the raw walked path (the acceptance band is +-0.75 m; robot half-width 0.29 m + walker sway).

trail_zone_connect_max_step_m.why: Trail exemption requires 8-neighbour connectivity with <=0.28 m changes, using the confirmed riser capability (measured maximum 0.27707 m in flight 2). Connectivity alone is insufficient: cross grade or independently measured tread capability must also pass.

trail_zone_max_cross_grade_deg.why: Restore the v7 trail exemption cross-track guard at 35 degrees. It prevents a nearby steep bank from receiving the generic trail prior. At narrow stairs the fit can include that bank; directly observed tread layers are assessed separately, without raising this guard.

cross_grade_half_width_m.why: Fix B: cross-track grade = least-squares plane over a rectangle centred on the cell, aligned with the route heading, extending the robot half-width 0.29 m on each side across the route (the roll the robot body experiences between its left and right contacts).

cross_grade_half_length_m.why: Fix B: along-route half extent of that rectangle = robot half-length 0.515 m, so the plane spans >= 2 treads (tread 0.30-0.50 m) and a single riser edge does not dominate the fit (v5: a 0.3 m-radius disc gave 36-54 deg at riser edges on the bends of s 5-21).

trail_tread_support.why: Round-2 raw cloud at s 5.2-6.9 m shows horizontal stair treads next to a steep bank. Fitting both together overestimates tread grade/step. In the connected trail zone only, extract observed near-horizontal layers within one 0.28 m riser above ground (5 cm lower noise tolerance), then require <=0.28 m tread-to-tread discontinuity and <=47 deg plane fit over 1 m. No ground, unknown, deck or obstacle reference is rewritten.

tread_max_normal_grade_deg.why: Reuse the existing deck surface-identification normal criterion (cos 35 deg) to separate tread returns from the adjacent steep bank and vertical riser faces. This is a surface selector, not a new locomotion limit; require the existing >=2 returns in a 5 cm coherent layer, and both capability checks afterward.

body_band_m.why: Collision capability is >0.30 and <0.80 m above OWN-cell ground (0.30 = confirmed 0.28 m riser + existing 0.02 m noise), matching sensor obstacle height. Keep the original geometry-band terrain-face exclusion (>0.22 m above max-known 3x3 ground). A higher neighbour must not lend its full height to a tall object: round-1 audit found 77 vanished components with own-ground returns up to 0.799 m. Classify from the fixed geometry band, and retain established hard objects with any own-ground-above-cutoff return.

body_min_points.why: Old proxy: >=2 returns in the body band of a 0.1 m column (single returns are noise).

vertical_normal_max_abs_nz.why: |normal_z|<0.35 (normal within ~20 deg of horizontal) = vertical surface (trunk, wall, post, rock face).

continuation_top_m.why: Continuation test = returns directly above the robot height (0.8-1.2 m) in the same 0.1 m column: trunks/posts/shrubs continue upward, grass does not; overhanging canopy higher than 1.2 m is ignored.

subbin_m.why: Fixed geometry evidence resolution ~0.097 m over 0.22-0.80 m (6 bins, as v7); not re-binned when collision capability changes.

linear_structure_classes.why: Classification codes that are empirically thin vertical/linear structures along the trail (posts, handrails; see classes.json). Used only as HARD evidence, never to make anything soft.

pca_block_cells.why: Fixed shape evidence in 0.3 x 0.3 m voxels, original geometry-band halves 0.22-0.51 and 0.51-0.80 m. True point x/y; same physical evidence thresholds.

pca_min_points.why: Minimum returns per voxel for a covariance estimate; sparser voxels give no soft evidence (conservative).

linear_min.why: Linearity (l1-l2)/l1 >= 0.7 with a near-vertical main axis = post/trunk/pole.

vertical_axis_min_abs_z.why: Main axis within ~37 deg of vertical.

planar_min.why: Planarity (l2-l3)/l1 >= 0.5: a surface. With a near-horizontal normal = wall/rock face/trunk; with scatter < soft_min_scattering = any solid surface (rock top, bench, ledge).

vertical_plane_max_normal_z.why: Plane normal within ~17 deg of horizontal.

continuous_column_min_vertical_fraction.why: A column occupied in all 6 sub-bins, continuing above 0.8 m and with >=50% vertical normals is a solid upright (trunk/post/wall).

soft_min_scattering.why: Soft requires volumetric scatter l3/l1 >= 0.1 (not a surface or a line).

soft_requires_no_body_top_continuation.why: Conservative: anything that continues above the robot height (0.8-2.0 m) in the same column is hard (shrubs with woody stems, trunks).

sparse_class.why: Fix A: obstacle cells with no hard evidence, not adjacent (3x3) to a hard-evidence cell and with a peak sub-bin return count below the solid-consistent density at their range are 'sparse': visible (flag 2, like soft) but non-colliding. v5 made them hard by default (no voxel had pca_min_points).

solid_density_reference.why: Fix A: reference population for solid density = obstacle cells passing the per-cell continuous-column test (all 6 sub-bins occupied, continuation above 0.8 m, >= 50 % vertical normals: trunks, posts, walls). The other hard evidence (vertical line/plane, surface) is decided per 0.3 m voxel and inherited by all 9 cells, including edge cells with 1-2 returns: their per-cell p10 is 2-3 at every range (= the body_min_points floor) and carries no density information; railing codes are thin rails/posts. Cross-check: the reference p10 within 1.5 m (13/12/10 returns per sub-bin) matches the bare-ground p10 within +-5 cm of the ground (9/12/12 per 0.1 m cell) - a solid face is sampled like ground.

solid_density_percentile.why: Fix A: a cell is solid-consistent if its peak sub-bin return count (0.1 x 0.1 x 0.097 m sub-voxel) reaches the 10th percentile of the reference cells at the same range: 90 % of verified solid columns pass. Sensitivity (v5 map): p5 / p10 / p25 leave 84 / 78 / 72 blocking stations (fix A alone).

solid_density_range_bins_m.why: Fix A: range proxy = distance to the walked (scanner) line; bins 0.5 m wide within 2 m (where footprints are evaluated), wider beyond. Cells beyond 12 m use the last bin. The threshold is forced non-increasing with range (return density can only fall with range).

solid_density_min_reference_cells.why: Fix A: a bin needs >= 50 reference cells (p10 rank >= 5) for a stable percentile; bins with fewer take the value of the nearest valid bin.

distance_method.why: v7: points uses Euclidean XY distance from each grid centre to the nearest body-band return in a colliding cell. Classification, ground-relative body band and walked-corridor mask remain unchanged. grid selects the v6 signed EDT of occupied cells. XY is the horizontal collision clearance of the 1.03 x 0.58 m envelope.

distance_noise_m.why: Reuse the existing 2 cm ground/range noise estimate in obstacles.body_band_m.why (0.20 m step + 0.02 m noise), consistent with ground.layer_thickness_m.why: 5 cm is about 2-3 sigma on hard surfaces. Outside occupied cells subtract 0.02 m from nearest collision-point XY distance. Inside a cell containing collision points use minus the centre-to-nearest-point distance (at least float32 epsilon); an unsigned point cloud does not identify a solid interior. This internal sign convention retains occupied cells without inflating them by half a grid; bilinear zero contours still have residual grid-phase error.

geometry_band_m.why: Keep v7 shape, continuity and density evidence in the original 0.22-0.80 m band, independent of the 0.30 m collision cutoff. Round 1 erased 347 old components despite remaining above-cutoff returns by changing PCA/sub-bin/reference populations. Classify from >=2 geometry returns, then collide only where at least one classified-object return exceeds the new cutoff. This conservatively retains established evidence without restoring low collision points.

halfwidth_m.why: Brief default: a person (shoulder ~0.45 m) physically passed within +-0.30 m of the raw scanner path.

apply_in_saved_map.why: map.npz layer 5/6 use the prior (variant c); variant b (no prior) is kept in aux.npz and reported.

source.value: raw 10 Hz poses inside segment A (incl. pruned back-and-forth)
source.why: The surveyor walked all of them.

width_clip_m.why: Brief: corridor width = measured feasible width clipped to [1,3] m; layer 3 = distance to centreline - width/2.

lateral_search_m.why: Feasible-width measurement: robot centre offsets within +-1.5 m (same as qualify_routes) at 0.05 m.

acceptance_band_m.why: Brief: continuous path must stay within +-0.75 m of the centreline.

fit_margin_m.why: User: report where feasible width < 0.58 m + 0.10 m margin.

dp_max_shift_per_station_m.why: Path search: lateral change <= 0.10 m per 0.2 m station (<= 27 deg off the route heading); extracted path is re-validated with fine + swept footprints using its own heading.

riser_min_m.why: A riser is a rise/fall >= 8 cm within ~0.1-0.3 m along the centreline profile (well above the ~1-2 cm ground noise, below any real stair riser 0.10-0.20 m).

riser_max_run_m.why: The rise must happen within 0.35 m along the route (a vertical-ish face, allowing an oblique crossing); slower rises are grade, not steps.

tread_max_m.why: Consecutive risers further apart than 1.2 m along the route belong to different flights.

min_risers.why: A flight needs >= 3 risers in the same direction.

sections.why: Cross-sections: deterministic picks from the old-proxy diagnosis (longest failing run per cause, narrowest lane, stairs) - listed in report.json.

fix_sections_s_m.why: Brief (fixes A-D): cross-sections at these scanner-centreline stations -> figures/fix_sections_sNNN.png, after (fixes) vs before (v5).

route._doc: Fix D: saved route = smoothed swept-feasible path within +-acceptance_band_m of the scanner centreline (nav4/mapping/route.py).

min_turn_radius_m.why: Omnidirectional wheel-legged base: the tracker (nav4/config/env.json) turns at <= max_yaw_rate 0.75 rad/s, so a 1.0 m radius is followed at 0.75 m/s (~ the 0.8 m/s speed limit) and at the 0.28 m/s stair speed a 0.37 m radius would do; 1.0 m therefore never limits the speed. The scanner centreline itself has 17 stations below 1.0 m (pause kinks, min 0.45 m at s 542.4).

station_spacing_m.why: Map contract: stations every 0.2 m of route arc length (uniform spacing L/round(L/0.2) so both end points are kept).

pull_scale_m.why: Smoothing = curvature energy + weak pull to the middle of the feasible tube; the pull acts on lateral scales longer than ~1 m (robot length), curvature dominates below. mu = 1/pull_scale^4.

repair_halfwindow_m.why: Where the path's own-heading footprint or swept check fails (or the radius is below the minimum), the tube is narrowed by 0.05 m (or the curvature weight raised x10) within +-0.6 m (~ robot half-length + one station) and the smoothing repeated.

max_iterations.why: Repair rounds; the history is reported in metadata route_adaptation.

blocked_freedom_m.why: At stations with no feasible offset (reported as blocked) the route is not pinned to the least-violating DP offset (which zig-zags by 0.05 m steps) but may move +-0.1 m (2 offset steps) around it so the curvature stays bounded; the place stays reported as blocked.

reweight_rounds.why: The quadratic energy sum |D2 P|^2/h^3 equals the curvature energy only at the nominal station spacing h; lateral offsets compress the spacing inside bends (a curve moved toward its centre of curvature would look 'smoother'). 4 reweighting rounds with w_i = (h/h_i)^3 make the energy track sum kappa^2 h_i.

refine_passes.why: Pass 1 builds the feasible tube with the robot aligned to the scanner centreline; the route's own heading differs by up to ~15 deg, which matters where the tube is one or two 0.05 m offsets wide. Pass 2 recomputes the tube around the pass-1 route with its own heading and re-smooths.

refine_halfwidth_m.why: Pass 2 is a refinement: offsets within +-0.25 m of the pass-1 route (and within +-0.75 m of the centreline), so it cannot jump to a different lane.
